subject: Post-call: MapStream deployment & SLO qualification
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@mapstream.ai>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@mapstream.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: MapStream deployment & SLO qualification

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same frame. Notes below are intentionally concise; attached is the SLO worksheet and the topology sketch we drew during the call.

Key pain / goals you shared
- Real-time geospatial inference for routing alerts; goal is P95 < 200ms for 256-token prompt generation (real-time scoring path).
- Peak sustained throughput target: ~80 req/s per region during peak business hours; baseline ~15 req/s off-peak.
- Hard constraint: customer-facing inference must not leave US data centers (data residency).
- Cost sensitivity around token-level spend; willingness to accept model quantization if quality delta < 2% on our evals.

Model & quality demands
- Preferred candidate: open 13B model (we discussed 13B-moderate with int8 quantization) — latency/accuracy trade-offs to validate.
- You will provide a 200-sample evaluation set and key prompts (Samira) for automated evaluation; we'll run A/B on quantized vs full-precision.

SLO mapping we recommend (to validate in POC)
- Latency: P95 <= 200ms (256 tokens), P99 <= 400ms (for highest-priority routes)
- Throughput: sustained 80 req/s regional (burst to 120 req/s for 5m)
- Availability: 99.9% regional SLA for the active region; cross-region failover plan for DR.

Proposed deployment topology (see attached sketch)
- Active-active across us-west2 (primary) and us-east4 (secondary) with smart routing based on latency and cost.
- Each region: 4 dedicated GPU workers (A100/RTX-class) with autoscaling to handle bursts.
- Prefix KV caching for repeated prompts; separate cache per region to comply with residency rule.
- Fallback model variant: 7B quantized small-latency model for non-blocking degradations.

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses)
1) You to share the 200-sample eval set and one-week traffic histogram (Samira) — target: EOD Fri 3/31.
2) Redwood to run quick quant vs fp eval and send back scorecard + latency sweep (Karthik) — ETA: 3 business days after samples.
3) Pre-provision regional test capacity and share access for smoke tests (Grace) — ETA: 4/5.
4) Confirm contract/compliance questions (Liam) — we flagged data residency and audit log retention; Redwood to supply SOC2 artefacts and retention options.

Attachments: MAPSTREAM_SLO_SHEET.xlsx (SLO matrix), mapstream_deploy_sketch.png (topology).

If any of this reads incorrectly, please flag. Otherwise I propose we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the evaluation results week of 4/8.

—

Thanks, Irene — super helpful recap and yes, aligns with our notes. A couple clarifications and one ask: 

Clarifications:
- The P95 target of 200ms is for the full scoring path (model inference + network). Our internal telemetry suggests we need model-only P95 <= 150ms to allow headroom. Please call that out in the scorecard.
- Peak 80 req/s per region is correct; we run regional routing by customer geography.

Ask:
- We can share the 200-sample eval set by EOD Friday (3/31). Also attaching an anonymized 7-day tail traffic CSV (we'll send as separate upload to your Drive link).

Compliance note: we cannot permit any persistent replication of user-identifying metadata outside our VPC. We are happy to do an API-based test with Redwood Private in our account or a Redwood-hosted instance in a US-only region. Which approach do you recommend for the POC?

Thanks — Samira

Appreciate the clarifications, Samira — answering inline and listing immediate asks from our side.

- Model-only P95 target: noted. We'll produce a latency sweep where model-only P95 target aimed at <= 140–150ms for the 256-token workload. We'll include token-count breakdowns (64/128/256).

POC recommendation (compliance):
- Given the residency requirement and the 'no persistent replication' constraint, I recommend Redwood Private deployed into MapStream's VPC for the POC (we can do a temporary image and remote support). This gives you control over ingress/egress and KMS while letting us run the kernel/quant checks. If you'd rather, we can instead provision a Redwood-hosted environment strictly in our us-west2 region and sign a short-term data-residency addendum. Both are doable; we lean to Private for fastest end-to-end parity.

Immediate asks from Redwood (to unblock):
1) Samira: share the 200-sample prompt set and the anonymized 7-day tail CSV link (as noted).
2) Grace: provision 2x A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west2 for initial latency profiling. (Grace: can you confirm by EOD 4/1?)
3) Irene/Karthik: we'll prepare the quantized vs FP runbook and required metrics (latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, quality delta).

I'll pick this up as the lead on the evaluation runs and send an initial scorecard within 72 hours of receiving samples + test capacity.
